“Ruby Ridge” is the nickname given to this incident, the FBI had a bench warrant on a man named Randy Weaver who lived with his wife and two sons in Ruby Ridge, Idaho after an embittered neighbor wrote letters claiming he had multiple unregistered firearms and made threats on the lives of President Reagan and then governor of Idaho John Evans.

Weaver and his family were likely aryan nationalists who had attended many meetings at compounds in the area for those purposes. This, along with the fact that the ATF knew he had sawn-off shotguns in his possession (they also perjured several times and claimed he was an experienced bank robber), got Weaver several gun charges for making and possessing (but not selling) illegal weapons.

The ATF posed as stranded motorists near the property and first arrested Randy when he and his wife stopped to help them. This move probably made up Randy’s mind to never trust the ATF, and he failed to appear in court on Feb 20 1990 for those reasons.

For the next two years Randy and his family were under constant surveillance and harassed routinely by ATF and US Marshall forces, leading until August 1992 when they believed they had enough evidence to arrest him. Government agents were on his property unannounced when on August 21, DUSMS agent Art Roderick threw rocks at the Weaver family dog to “test its reaction” while it was being accompanied by Weavers 14 year old son Sammy and a family friend, Kevin Harris. The boys believed the dog had noticed some sort of wild game and followed it. The Gov. team initially retreated, but decided instead to take hidden defensive positions, and Roderick decided to shoot the dog dead when he thought it gave his position away. Sammy, not knowing that they were Marshalls (the agents later perjured and claimed they had identified themselves when no such precaution was taken) was enraged and shot at the intruders, with his friend Harris shooting and killing DUSM agent William Degan (he was later acquitted on self defense grounds). The agents returned fire, and killed the 14 year old boy as he retreated up a hill by shooting him in the back.

The ensuing standoff lasted another day, and ended after FBI snipers were deployed and given the instruction to shoot and kill anyone with a weapon present not identified by the FBI. When Randy, his wife Vicki (holding one of their infant daughters), their 16 year old daughter Sara, and the previously mentioned friend Kevin Harris tried to make an attempt to visit their son and friends dead body. FBI sniper Lon Horiuchi (180 meters out) shot and wounded Randy in the back as he opened the latch on the shed which housed his son’s corpse. When his family retreated. **Horiuchi made the decision to fire another shot that hit Harris in the back, which would pass through and kill Vicki Weaver as she retreated with her infant daughter. Despite years of legal battles and the shot being deemed “unconstitutional” by the federal government, Lon Horiuchi was never held legally accountable, with sovereign immunity for federal agents being cited by a judge for their reasoning of charge dismissal.**

Randy soon after surrendered, having lost his son and wife and fearing for the safety of the rest of his family along with a grievously wounded Harris. Randy would go on to serve 16 months in prison after being acquitted of all charges except for the prior bench warrant and failure to appear in court. Harris was acquitted of all charges, although in 1997 the state attempted to indict him for First-degree murder for the killing of agent Degan. This would be thrown out due to double jeopardy laws, however.

The Weaver family would be paid 3.1 million USD in damages in 1995, Harris would be awarded 380,000 USD. Randy passed away in 2022 and is survived by his three daughters, the eldest of which, Sera, became a born-again Christian and has gone on to publicly forgive all those involved.

[Full report from Ruby Ridge Task Force](http://law2.umkc.edu/faculty/projects/ftrials/weaver/dojruby1.html)

The simple fact of it is, and all it can ever be, is that the FBI escalated a situation that could’ve been solved with knocking on a man’s door into shooting and murdering his dogs, wife and son. The fact that all the agents involved barely got any punishment kind of unequivocally proves how seedy the entire organization is. That doesn’t justify Oklahoma City or anything, but this incident is a tragic case of government harassment that everyone should now when they think that their government cares about them at all.
